title: CLAUDE.md
text: R package joint modeling longitudinal biomarker trajectories time--event outcomes using ODEs. Biomarker dynamics follow second-order linear ODE solved via matrix exponential (Cayley-Hamilton), linked Cox proportional hazards model B-spline baseline hazard. Estimation uses TMB (Template Model Builder) automatic differentiation Laplace approximation random effects.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Solved analytically via Cayley-Hamilton: exp(·dt) decomposed using discriminant characteristic equation. Uses CppAD::CondExpGt select REAL (D>0) COMPLEX (D<0) branches without breaking AD tape — branches always computed, selected via CondExp. enables AD branch changes dynamics RE modify eigenvalues optimization.

Formula random effects add heterogeneity dynamic log-coefficients /forcing function. example, (1 + biomarker + velocity | id) uses \mathbf{b}_i = \begin{pmatrix} b_{m0,} & b_{v0,} & b_{\omega,} & b_{d,} & b_{f0,} \end{pmatrix}^{\top} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b), b_{m0,} b_{v0,} perturb initial state, b_{\omega,} perturbs \theta_{\omega }, b_{d,} perturbs \theta_{d }, b_{f0,} random forcing intercept. formula operator controls covariance structure: | estimates full covariance matrix || estimates independent diagonal covariance. title: Technical Details

title: Technical Details
text: ODE \ddot{m} = b_1 m + b_2 \dot{m} + f constant forcing [t, t{+}\Delta t] exact solution: \begin{pmatrix} m(t{+}\Delta t) \\ \dot{m}(t{+}\Delta t) \end{pmatrix} = \exp(\Delta t) \begin{pmatrix} m(t) \\ \dot{m}(t) \end{pmatrix} + \int_0^{\Delta t} \exp()\,ds \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ f \end{pmatrix} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ b_1 & b_2 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr) companion matrix. Cayley–Hamilton theorem, 2 \times 2 matrix characteristic polynomial \lambda^2 - b_2\lambda - b_1 = 0, matrix exponential can written \exp(\Delta t) = a_0 + a_1 scalar coefficients a_0, a_1. Expanding: \begin{pmatrix} m(t{+}\Delta t) \\ \dot{m}(t{+}\Delta t) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a_0 & a_1 \\ b_1 a_1 & a_0 + b_2 a_1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} m(t) \\ \dot{m}(t) \end{pmatrix} + f \begin{pmatrix} J_1 \\ a_1 \end{pmatrix} forcing integrals derived augmented 3 \times 3 system state (m, \dot{m}, f)^\top: position forcing integral J_1 = (a_0 - 1)/b_1, velocity forcing term simply f \cdot a_1 (can also verified differentiating position solution). coefficients a_0, a_1 depend eigenvalue structure. Let \mu = b_2\Delta t/2 (half-trace), D = b_2^2 + 4b_1 (discriminant), s^2 = D\Delta t^2/4: Underdamped (D < 0, \xi < 1): complex eigenvalues damped frequency \omega_d = \sqrt{-s^2}. a_0 = e^{\mu}(\cos\omega_d - \mu\,\text{sinc}(\omega_d)), \quad a_1 = e^{\mu}\Delta t\,\text{sinc}(\omega_d) \text{sinc}(x) = \sin(x)/x. Overdamped (D > 0, \xi > 1): two distinct real eigenvalues \delta = \sqrt{s^2}. a_0 = e^{\mu}(\cosh\delta - \mu\,\text{sinhc}(\delta)), \quad a_1 = e^{\mu}\Delta t\,\text{sinhc}(\delta) \text{sinhc}(x) = \sinh(x)/x. Critically damped (D = 0, \xi = 1): repeated eigenvalue. a_0 = e^{\mu}(1 - \mu), \quad a_1 = e^{\mu}\Delta t

title: Simulate Data from a Joint Ordinary Differential Equation Model — simulate
text: biomarker trajectory \(m_i(t)\) subject \(\) follows damped harmonic oscillator external forcing: $$\ddot{m}_i(t) + 2\xi\omega\dot{m}_i(t) + \omega^2 m_i(t) =   k \omega^2 [f_0 + \mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}_{exc}]$$ : \(\omega = 2\pi/T\) natural angular frequency \(\xi\) damping ratio determining oscillation behavior \(k\) scales excitation amplitude \(f_0\) constant excitation term \(\mathbf{X}_i\) contains time-invariant covariates \(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{exc}\) represents covariate effects excitation initial biomarker drawn population distribution: \(m_i(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{m,0}, \sigma_{m,0}^2)\) \(\dot{m}_i(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{v,0}, \sigma_{v,0}^2)\) observed longitudinal measurements incorporate additive Gaussian noise: $$y_{ij} = m_i(t_{ij}) + \epsilon_{ij}$$ \(\epsilon_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_\epsilon^2)\) represents independent measurement error.

title: Simulate Data from a Joint Ordinary Differential Equation Model — simulate
text: instantaneous hazard function incorporates current biomarker value velocity (power): $$\lambda_i(t) = \lambda_0(t)\exp(\alpha_1 m_i(t) +   \alpha_2[\dot{m}_i(t)]^\gamma + \mathbf{W}_i^T\boldsymbol{\phi})$$ : \(\lambda_0(t)\) denotes Weibull baseline hazard: \(\lambda_0(t) = (\kappa/\lambda)(t/\lambda)^{\kappa-1}\) \(\alpha_1\) quantifies association current biomarker value \(\alpha_2\) quantifies association biomarker velocity (power) \(\gamma \\{0, 1, 2\}\) determines power velocity: 0 (velocity effect), 1 (linear), 2 (quadratic) \(\mathbf{W}_i\) contains baseline covariates \(\boldsymbol{\phi}\) represents covariate effects survival

title: Simulate Data from a Joint Ordinary Differential Equation Model — simulate
text: function models patient heterogeneity continuous distributions dynamics parameters \(\xi_i\) (damping ratio) \(T_i\) (period): $$\xi_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\xi, \sigma_\xi^2), \quad   T_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_T, \sigma_T^2)$$ transformed ODE parameters via: $$\omega_i = 2\pi/T_i, \quad   \beta_{1,} = -\omega_i^2, \quad   \beta_{2,} = -2\xi_i\omega_i$$ transformation uses Delta method preserve correct covariance structure ODE parameter space. default simulation includes random effects initial biomarker, initial velocity, two dynamic log-coefficients, forcing intercept; forcing covariate coefficients shared fixed effects.
